script: Why did my husband walk back into his own funeral three years after I buried him? But grief wasn't what brought him back. Because he needed my signature on something. Three years ago his car was found burned at the bottom of a ravine, and the dental records matched. I collected eight hundred thousand dollars in life insurance and raised our son alone. At his own memorial, a man in a gray coat sat down beside me. He knew our son's middle name, and the song we danced to at our wedding. He said the accident had been real, just not for him. He needed me to sign papers declaring him alive again, because his new wife was pregnant and her insurance company was asking questions. I asked what would happen to the money I had already spent. He said that wasn't his problem anymore. And the question neither of us said out loud is the one I still can't answer.
